answer: To resist sybils, each agent continuously publishes hashed timber samples of its private decision traces onto a public ridge of sequential commitments. The ridge forms a unique horizon visible to all peers: any identity whose timber collides or fails sequential consistency is pruned. An attacker spinning up N identities must generate and maintain N independent, non-colliding timber streams forever; the compute and entropy cost scales linearly with the farm size while honest agents pay only once.
